daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Ridho Rahmadi, the son-in-law of prominent politician Amien Rais, has resigned as chairman of Partai Ummat. This represents a significant leadership change within the party founded by Amien Rais. The resignation comes amid broader political realignments in Indonesia's party landscape.

  • DPR Speaker Dasco Wardoyo pledged to resign if the Asset Forfeiture Bill is not passed by December 15, responding to demands from demonstrators who rallied in Jakarta on August 27.
  • The DPR explained why the Asset Forfeiture Bill has taken an extended period to finalize, amid public pressure to expedite its passage.
  • President Prabowo secured distribution of subsidised goods to ensure they reach the public, addressing concerns about access to basic necessities.
  • NU chairman Gus Yahya stated that NU cadres are people of integrity and will not be influenced by external intervention, speaking ahead of the organization's national congress.
  • Gus Yahya prepared an accountability report of nearly 1,000 pages for presentation at the NU Muktamar (national congress).
  • A meeting on procedural rules for the NU Muktamar will establish the mechanism for electing the next chairman of the PBNU executive board.
  • Former President Jokowi's legal team objected to withdrawal of a lawsuit concerning his academic credentials, requesting that the case proceed to trial.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Italian aircraft carrier Giuseppe Garibaldi will dock in Jakarta for a handover ceremony to formally transfer the vessel to Indonesia. This marks a significant milestone in Indonesia's naval modernization efforts, following the purchase of the former Italian flagship. The arrival of the carrier has sparked debate about whether it should serve merely as a symbol of national pride or deliver substantive capabilities.

  • The DPR gave approval to sell KRI Ki Hajar Dewantara after the vessel served nearly five decades in the Indonesian Navy.
  • Indonesia's Foreign Ministry expressed condolences over flash floods at the Nepal-China border that killed hundreds.
  • The Ministry of Foreign Affairs urged Indonesian citizens in Nepal to remain vigilant and comply with local authorities following the devastating flash floods.
  • The TNI Air Force explained the early morning flight of three F-16 fighter jets over the Monas area in central Jakarta on Friday.
  • Foreign Minister Sugiono pushed for pencak silat to be featured at the 2032 Brisbane Olympics, promoting Indonesia's traditional martial art on the global stage.

Other

The DPR approved Destry Damayanti as the new governor of Bank Indonesia, confirming her appointment to lead the country's central bank. This appointment comes at a crucial time as Indonesia navigates economic pressures and seeks to maintain monetary stability. The fintech company Ajaib received an investment injection of Rp 4.8 trillion from SBI Holdings.

  • State investment holding company Danantara eyes wider data center investment as demand for digital infrastructure surges across the archipelago.
  • Jakarta Governor Pramono offered 37 investment projects worth Rp 115 trillion to potential investors in the capital.
  • The Indonesian Commission for Child Protection (KPAI) urged the government to take forest fires more seriously in protecting children from the health impacts of haze and smoke.
  • Indonesia's Ministry of Immigration will use AI and drones to monitor foreign nationals operating in the country, enhancing oversight of expatriate activities.
  • Health Minister tightened screening of volunteers to prevent further deaths at disaster sites, following recent fatalities among relief workers.
